mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting returning pollinators with spreading mammals was most worthwhile: it brought pollination, fruit and feeding together as a functioning food web, rather than simply adding species.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting returning fruit and tree dwellers in succession yielded no partners, making the search for the last connection a little repetitive.

surprise.text: The familiar insects-and-flowers pairing was unavailable at first; the woodland had to recover before insects could return as pollinators.

arbitrary.text: The initial restriction on combining insects with flowers felt unclear until the recovery sequence gave the insects a role. I understood the ecological story afterward, but not why the earlier pairing was unavailable.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what the recovered world makes next: the chapter connected ecological processes clearly while acknowledging that extinct lineages cannot be restored.
